$comment: Curation for `python -m pipelines mountains` (see harim_reconcile.py for the rules). Every text claim has a `source` URL and a `quote`; the run re-checks each quote against the cached source and fails if it is missing. Edit, re-run, review data/mountains_review_report.md.

BDI.reason: The Factbook's "unnamed elevation on Mukike Range 2,685 m" is Mount Heha (2,684 m in Wikidata), which Wikipedia names as Burundi's highest mountain.
BDI.quote: Mount Heha is the highest mountain in Burundi

BEN.reason: Mont Sokbaro (658 m) is Wikidata's high point and is mostly cited as Benin's highest point.
BEN.review: Contested: satellite (SRTM) data puts an unnamed point near Kotopounga higher (672 m per Wikipedia; 675 m per the Factbook).
BEN.quote: This designation is contested, as SRTM readings

BWA.reason: Wikidata's P610 names Otse Hill (1,491 m), but its own elevations, the Factbook ("Manyelanong Hill 1,495 m") and Wikipedia put Monalanong Hill (1,494 m) highest.
BWA.review: Otse Hill (1,491 m, a surveyed trigonometrical station) is also often cited as Botswana's highest point.
BWA.quote: Monalanong Hill is a mountain often considered the highest point of Botswana

CMR.reason: The Factbook's "Fako on Mont Cameroun" is the higher of Mount Cameroon's two peaks.
CMR.quote: Fako (the name of the higher of its two peaks)

GMB.reason: Wikidata has no P610 high point for The Gambia; Sare Firasu Hill (51 m) is the highest mapped feature.
GMB.review: The Factbook gives an unnamed 63 m elevation 3 km southeast of Sabi instead; The Gambia's true high point needs verification.

GNB.reason: Wikidata's P610 points to a "Monte Torin" item on the northern border; the Monte Torin that Wikipedia describes (266 m, near the southern border with Guinea) is a separate item, used here.
GNB.review: The Factbook gives Dongol Ronde (277 m) as Guinea-Bissau's highest point instead.
GNB.quote: Monte Torin is the highest point of Guinea-Bissau

MUS.reason: The Factbook's "Mont Piton 828 m" is Piton de la Petite Rivière Noire (828 m).

SDN.reason: The Factbook's "Jabal Marrah 3,042 m" is the Jebel Marra massif, whose highest point is Deriba Caldera.
SDN.quote: The highest point is Deriba Caldera.

SEN.reason: Wikidata's P610 (Népin Cliff, 531 m) has no coordinates; the Factbook's "unnamed elevation 2.8 km southeast of Nepen Diaka 648 m" matches Wikidata's 648 m Nepen Diakha.
SEN.review: Named after the nearby village of Nepen Diakha; the point itself is unnamed.

CPV.reason: Wikidata gives the Pedra de Lume salt ponds (30 m below sea level); the Factbook gives the Atlantic Ocean (sea level).
CPV.review: The cited Wikipedia article on Pedra de Lume does not state its elevation; the below-sea-level value needs verification.

ERI.reason: The Factbook's "near Kulul within the Danakil Depression" (−75 m) is Lake Kulul (−75 m in Wikidata).

MRT.reason: Sebkha de Ndrhamcha (Wikidata) and Sebkhet Te-n-Dghamcha (Factbook) are spellings of the same salt flat.

TCD.reason: The Factbook's "Djourab" is the desert containing the Bodélé Depression, Chad's lowest point.
TCD.quote: Its bottom lies about 155 meters above sea level.

UGA.reason: Wikidata gives Lake Albert; the Factbook gives the Albert Nile (614 m), the river leaving the lake.
UGA.review: The Factbook's Albert Nile (614 m) may be lower than Lake Albert; Uganda's lowest point needs verification.
